name: Swim: Rhythm Drills
description: Two drills for a kick that rides the roll instead of running as a separate motor. Grab them on their own, or as the middle block of the full session.
flowNotes: **Your arms and legs are not supposed to be synced to each other — they are both synced to your hips.** Your roll is already a hip rotation, and the kick is a hip movement too. Same joint, same motion. These two drills strip the stroke down far enough that you can feel one drive the other.

flowSequence.notes:
🔆 **Six kicks lying on your side. Then ONE stroke, which rolls you onto the other side. Then six kicks there.** Repeat down the length. It is the 6-3-6 drill with the three strokes cut to one, so there is nowhere to hide the switch.
- **The single stroke IS the drill.** The six kicks are the rest; the switch is the rep.
- **As you take that stroke your body rolls — let the kick fire WITH the roll.** One roll, one kick. You are not timing legs against arms; you are letting the rotation you are already doing carry the kick.
- **The fault to catch: the kick going quiet during the switch.** That is the two-separate-programs habit, and the switch is exactly where the kick should be strongest. If it dies there, slow the whole drill down until it doesn't.
- **Don't count the kick or force a beat.** Let the switch set the timing and the rhythm shows up on its own.
- **Same side position as the side-kick drill** — bottom arm long and slightly down, head in line with your spine, face at the side wall, lower goggle wet.
- Breathe during the six kicks, not during the switch.

**Normal freestyle using one arm only. The other arm stays stretched out in front the whole length**, not resting at your side — that long lead arm is what keeps your legs up.
- **Half the arm information, so the pairing is easy to feel:** one arm pulls, one kick lands. That is the whole point of doing it one-armed.
- Breathe toward the arm that is working.
- **Still driven from the hips.** The pull doesn't start at the shoulder — you roll, and the arm and the kick both come off that roll.
- Slow. This is a feel drill, not a swim.

tips: Arms don't sync to legs. Both sync to your hips.
If the kick goes quiet during the switch, slow the drill down rather than trying harder.
Drills go first, while you're fresh.
Rest at the wall until your breathing settles, however long that takes.
